newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Short-covering boosts SIMEX JGB, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Short-covering boosts SIMEX JGB, more gains seen.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rallied sharply on Friday in a bout of short-covering as dealers reassessed the implications of the Bank of Japan's tankan report.
The report, published on Wednesday, showed an unexpectedly optimistic outlook for large manufacturers and exporters.
Bond and Euroyen futures fell into a tailspin on fears of a possible interest rate rise.
But dealers said these worries had been overplayed and most non-Japanese investors doubted Japanese rates would rise before the first quarter of next year.
"Interest rate policy is clearly not going to change in the next few weeks -- probably not this year," said one dealer.
"I think a few people went short in JGBs on Wednesday and now they have squared off positions," he added.
The September SIMEX JGB futures contract closed at 124.18, up 0.87, after opening at 123.30.
In the medium term, several dealers felt the September JGB contract could rise towards 125.
SIMEX Euroyen futures followed the JGBs higher with back months gaining most.
The September 1998 Euroyen contract rose 0.11 to 98.48 by 1115 GMT, up sharply from its IMM close at 98.35.
Dealers said the contract implied a 45-basis point rise in Japanese interest rates, generally in line with most economists' expectations of a 50-basis point jump early in 1998.
The March 1998 Euroyen contract was up 0.09 by 1115 GMT at 98.86, against its IMM close of 98.75.
Eurodollar futures were flat. September Eurodollars closed at 94.130, unchanged from the IMM close.
